verdict: Panel says Liverpool were denied a penalty at Arsenal. Injury worries remain.

big.label: KMI panel vote: Isak foul was a penalty

posters.headline: Panel: Liverpool denied a penalty
posters.summary: The KMI Panel says Timber's tug on Isak should have been a penalty in the 1-0 loss to Arsenal.

read.what: ESPN reports the five-person panel voted 4:1 that referee Andy Madley was wrong not to award a penalty for Jurrien Timber's shirt-tug on Alexander Isak at Anfield on 1 November. Arsenal won 1-0. Three said VAR Stuart Attwell should have sent Madley to the pitchside screen.
read.context: Arsenal lead the table on 27 points, Liverpool are fourth on 18. The panel only explains decisions. It changes no result or points.
read.take: Opinion: the verdict backs Liverpool's complaint, but it cannot give back the points. Two panellists felt VAR should stay out, so the call was not unanimous. Watch for any PGMOL response.

posters.headline: Szoboszlai knee waits on Hungary
posters.summary: Hungary say a decision on the knee sprain will almost certainly come at the last minute.

read.what: Sports Mole says Szoboszlai hurt his knee in the 3-1 win at Palace and Hungary call it a sprain. Their statement says he has had medical examinations and a decision on playing 'will almost certainly only be made at the last minute'. Hungary play Georgia on Saturday.
read.context: Liverpool host Man United on Sunday 22 November. Van Dijk and Gravenberch are also doubts, so midfield and defence are thin.
read.take: Opinion: Liverpool would want him rested, not risked. No club statement is quoted, so the recovery time is unknown. Watch whether he plays on Saturday.

stories.headline: Man United agree Pochettino in principle
stories.summary: Sky says United have a verbal agreement in principle. Carrick is likely to go first. Not official.

read.what: Sky reports a 'verbal agreement in principle' with Mauricio Pochettino, conditional on Michael Carrick being removed. United still need to agree a £7m buyout with US Soccer. Sky says it is understood, with no club statement.
read.context: United visit Anfield on 22 November. Pochettino may coach the USA in the break, so he could have little time with the squad.
read.take: Opinion: Sky's report is strong but not a done deal until United confirm. A new manager makes United harder to predict. Watch for an official announcement.

nextMatch.teamNews: Van Dijk, Szoboszlai doubts; Gravenberch major doubt; Frimpong out. Sky lists 16:00 and 16:30.

tracker.update: No change. A report of an agreed deal is unconfirmed; The Athletic says talks may take time.

talking.headline: KMI panel: Isak foul should be a penalty
talking.summary: Panel voted 4:1 the Timber tug on Isak was a foul. Arsenal won 1-0 on 1 November.
talking.for: Liverpool: the panel agrees the challenge met the holding threshold and three said VAR should have intervened. Iraola says players must go down or nothing is given.
talking.against: Two panellists felt the high bar for VAR was not met because impact is subjective. Arsenal's win stands and the panel changes no result.
talking.take: Opinion: the ruling shows the system is inconsistent, but a late verdict helps nobody. The 3 to 2 split on VAR shows how thin the line is.
